**Given** the bookmark button's four states (idle/saving/saved/error, UX-DR6)
**When** I tap a message already in the `saved` state
**Then** it is a no-op — the backend returns 200, not 409, and no duplicate Entry is ever created (FR-29 idempotency).

**Given** a save fails
**When** the error state shows
**Then** the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable and the button resets to a retryable state rather than freezing (FR-30).
**And** state is carried by icon + color together on the bookmark button, never color alone (UX-DR6, Accessibility Floor).

### Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation

As a user,
I want the assistant to occasionally point out a pattern in my own writing without me having to ask,
So that the memory the product promises actually becomes visible to me.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** either 5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity (whichever occurs first) within the active Chat Session
**When** that condition is satisfied
**Then** `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` injects an Insight once per satisfied condition — never both, never twice for the same window.

**Given** the Insight card (ochre spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x," UX-DR5)
**When** it appears
**Then** it is interleaved into the chat stream as the only accent-colored element inside it.

**Given** Insight generation fails
**When** the failure occurs
**Then** it is handled fire-and-forget via the `isolatedSideEffect` helper from Story 6.4 (AD-13) — the composer remains enabled, no error overlay appears, and ordinary chat messages (Story 6.1) keep working uninterrupted.

**Given** an Insight is visible
**When** I dismiss it
**Then** scroll position and all other conversation state are unaffected.
**And** this Insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from Story 6.1, never a parallel `Resource<T>` (AD-12).

## Epic 7: Personal Summary Export

Users can request a narrative PDF + raw-data export for any date period, and always get their raw data even if the AI-generated narrative fails or the period turns out to be empty.

### Story 7.1: Request a Period Export & Job Status Tracking

As a user,
I want to request an export for a chosen date period and see its progress,
So that I know what's happening while a narrative + data package is being prepared.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** I tap the download icon on Meus Registros and select a period
**When** I confirm
**Then** `POST /export/summary` creates the job and the export sheet opens (UX-DR15, `radiusLg`/`elevation2`).

**Given** the job is in progress
**When** I poll via `GET /export/:jobId/status`
**Then** the sheet reflects exactly five states — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio — reporting `status` (job) and `narrativeStatus` (AI summary) independently.

**Given** a stage changes
**When** the sheet updates
**Then** it replaces its content in place — the sheet itself never closes and reopens mid-job.

### Story 7.2: Narrative-Independent Raw-Data Download

As a user,
I want my raw data available as soon as it's ready, even if the AI summary is still working or has failed,
So that my export is never held hostage by a model call.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** raw data finishes before the narrative
**When** this hybrid state occurs (`status=data_ready`, `narrativeStatus=processing`)
**Then** "Baixar dados brutos" is already enabled and downloadable via `GET /export/:jobId/download` while the summary-progress text keeps showing underneath — never withheld waiting on the narrative (UX-DR34).

**Given** the narrative step fails or is skipped
**When** the job otherwise completes (`status=done`)
**Then** "Baixar dados brutos" remains enabled and error copy is framed around the narrative only.

**Given** the narrative succeeds
**When** the job completes fully
**Then** "Resumo pronto" shows with both downloads (PDF narrative + raw data) available.

# Epic 6 Context: Conversational Memory, Save-to-Journal & Insights

<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->

## Goal

Users hold a persistent, multi-session conversation with an assistant whose answers are grounded in semantic retrieval over their own past Entries — not generic replies — can turn their own reflective chat messages into real journal Entries with one tap, and occasionally receive an unprompted insight about a pattern in their own writing. None of this (dropped streams, save failures, insight-generation failures) may ever block, corrupt, or freeze the core chat experience. This epic is the product's central differentiator: proving the memory-over-own-history bet end-to-end against the real backend.

## Stories

- Story 6.1: Send Message & Receive RAG-Grounded Streaming Response
- Story 6.2: Multi-Session Chat History & New Conversation
- Story 6.3: Dropped-Stream Resilience & Offline Composer Lock
- Story 6.4: Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry
- Story 6.5: Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation

## Requirements & Constraints

- Chat responses stream via SSE and must be grounded in retrieval over the user's own Entries; exactly three visible states exist for a response: streaming/processing, error, complete — no others.
- A Chat Message never auto-creates an Entry; saving one to the journal (this epic's story 6.4) is the sole explicit exception.
- A user holds multiple named Chat Sessions, switchable and startable from the side menu; starting a new session requires connectivity (blocked offline, consistent with the offline composer lock). A returning session restores its last scroll position.
- A dropped response stream keeps the partial message on screen with a failure indicator (never clears bubble content) and is recoverable via a dedicated retry call that regenerates without duplicating the original question.
- Offline disables the message composer (and the new-session entry point) with an offline banner, while existing history remains fully visible/scrollable.
- The save-to-journal (bookmark) affordance appears only on the user's own messages, never on AI responses; it creates an Entry carrying a reference back to the source chat message, through the same shared entries-feature use case introduced earlier in delivery — never by importing the entries repository/data source directly.
- Saving the same message twice is idempotent: no duplicate Entry, no conflict surfaced to the user (success, not error).
- A save failure never freezes the chat session or the button — the button returns to a retryable state and the rest of the session stays usable.
- An Insight is injected into the active session on exactly one trigger per satisfied window — either N user messages sent or a fixed inactivity timeout, whichever comes first — never both, never twice for the same window.
- An Insight-generation failure is silent to the user: no error overlay, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat keeps working. Insight quality/content is explicitly outside acceptance scope — only the trigger/injection/failure-isolation mechanism is graded.
- Dismissing an Insight never affects scroll position or any other conversation state.

## Technical Decisions

- Feature lives at `features/chat/`; it consumes `features/entries/`'s abstract save/create-entry port from `entries/domain` only — never anything from `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (layering invariant, zero violations tolerated).
- Repositories return `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`, except the chat response itself, which is `Stream<Either<Failure, T>>` given its SSE nature. The closed, 14-member `Failure` hierarchy (13 server codes + a local-only malformed-response code) is shared from `core/` and never redefined per feature.
- Chat holds no local write queue: a send attempted with no connectivity resolves immediately to a `networkOffline` failure, never queued. Plain history reads (sessions, messages) transparently fall back to the local cache; retry logic for retryable failure codes lives once in the shared API client, not reimplemented per feature.
- Chat's message/streaming state is its own sealed state class (append-only, streaming-aware) — explicitly excluded from the shared generic `Resource<T>` single-fetch state pattern, because it isn't a single fetch.
- The proactive-insight overlay is a value appended onto the existing chat state from story 6.1, never a second parallel state container.
- A never-throws `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` helper (`Future<Either<Failure, T>> Function(Future<T> Function())`-shaped) ships with this epic's first consumer (the save-to-journal story) and is reused unawaited (fire-and-forget) by the insight story so a slow/failed insight never blocks or delays the chat stream.
- No BLoC/Cubit ever takes another BLoC/Cubit as a constructor dependency, in this feature or across features; independent state sources compose via injected domain streams/use-cases or `BlocListener`, never a direct BLoC-to-BLoC reference.
- The entries-owning feature's save port is idempotent on the save-to-journal identifier at the implementation level (not just the type signature) — a repeat save for the same source message never creates a second Entry.
- Session/message/sync-badge local caching follows the same per-feature local-cache-box convention used by other features; cursor-based pagination for session and message lists follows the server's own cursor convention verbatim.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Chat bubbles: user (sage, squared bottom-right corner) vs. AI (ivory, squared bottom-left, resting elevation). A streaming AI bubble adds a blinking cursor at the text's end and nothing else changes visually while generating; under Reduce Motion the cursor blink is skipped and final text shows immediately instead.
- A dropped/failed response replaces the bubble's timestamp slot with red retry copy; bubble text itself is never cleared.
- Bookmark button: four states on every user message only — idle (outline) / saving (spinner, or a static label under Reduce Motion) / saved (ochre check) / error (red warning). Tapping an already-saved message is a no-op. State must be carried by icon + color together, never color alone. Tap target ≥44pt.
- Insight card: ochre left spine, mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" — the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself.
- Offline banner disables sending only; conversation history stays scrollable and readable underneath it. A session-expired overlay (re-auth) can appear over chat without losing scroll position or in-memory history.
- A new session opens with the composer focused and only the placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem..." — no invented greeting copy.
- No swipe gestures, no nested overlays, no pull-to-refresh beyond what the session/message endpoints already govern.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 6.1 establishes the chat stream/state machine that 6.2 (sessions), 6.3 (retry/offline), 6.4 (bookmark), and 6.5 (insight overlay) all build on or append to.
- Story 6.4 is this epic's (and the codebase's) first consumer of the shared `isolated_side_effect` helper; Story 6.5 reuses that same helper fire-and-forget.
- Story 6.4 depends on the entries feature's save/create-entry port already existing from earlier delivery work; it must not introduce a second entry model or reach into entries' data layer.
- Story 6.5's insight overlay is layered onto 6.1's chat state rather than a separate state container, so it cannot be built independently of 6.1's state shape.

1	---
2	title: 'Story 6.4 — Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-06'
5	status: 'done'
6	review_loop_iteration: 1
7	baseline_commit: '03b76ffef4d1896d48e591270aa05de464fd3abf'
8	context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
9	---
10	
11	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** A user's own reflective Chat Message can't become a journal Entry without retyping it — `ChatUiMessage` has no bookmark affordance, `EntriesRepository.create()` has no `chatMessageId` slot even though `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already reserve it, and `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` is still an `UnimplementedError` stub explicitly waiting for this story.
16	
17	**Approach:** Add a four-state (`idle`/`saving`/`saved`/`error`) bookmark button to user-only chat bubbles. `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage(messageId)` calls the real `isolatedSideEffect` (replacing the stub) wrapping a call to a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — the shared interface AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires — which itself wraps `EntriesRepository.create(..., source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: ...)`. `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under `entries/data`/`entries/presentation`.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- Bookmark affordance: `ChatMessageRole.user` bubbles only.
23	- `ChatCubit` depends on `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — never `EntriesRepository` directly, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (AGENTS.md: "RF10 must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly").
24	- Save runs through `isolatedSideEffect` (real body, replacing the `UnimplementedError` stub), awaited before bookmark state updates.
25	- Tapping `saved` is a client-side no-op; repeat backend calls for the same `chatMessageId` are themselves idempotent (200, not 409 — `openapi.yaml`'s `entries.create` doc) so no extra client dedup needed.
26	- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.
27	- Icon + color together, never color alone: `idle` outline, `saving` spinner (static label under Reduce Motion), `saved` ochre check (`colorAccent`, `0xFFC98A3E`), `error` red warning (`colorError`). Tap target ≥44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
28	- Bookmarking requires a non-null `serverId` (the id sent as `chatMessageId`); tapping before that is a no-op, mirroring `retryMessage`'s guard.
29	- Both of `bookmarkMessage`'s `emit()` calls (before and after the `isolatedSideEffect` await) check `isClosed` first — not just the one after the await.
30	- A bookmark glyph's Reduce-Motion static label sits in a width-capped slot (e.g. wrapped the same way `bubbleContainer` is `Flexible`-constrained), so it cannot squeeze the message bubble under large accessibility text scaling.
31	
32	**Ask First:** none — `chatMessageId` on `create()` is a pre-reserved slot (`Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already exist for this story), not a new architectural call.
33	
34	**Never:**
35	- Never import `EntriesRepository`, `entries/data/`, or `entries/presentation/` from `chat/` — only `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`.
36	- Never route the bookmark save through `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — its `create()` clears *any* app-wide failed pending-write on each call (written for exactly one capture flow in flight at a time), so a concurrent chat bookmark could silently clear an unrelated capture flow's visible error card.
37	- Never persist bookmark state across restarts — in-memory only; a stale `idle` post-reload is harmless given backend idempotency.
38	- Never let a bookmark failure disable the composer or affect other bubbles.
39	- Never introduce a second Entry model or bypass `EntriesRepository` (the use case's own only caller).
40	
41	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
42	
43	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
44	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
45	| Happy path | Tap bookmark on a user bubble with `serverId` set, `idle` | Bubble flips `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (ochre check); `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase(content, chatMessageId: serverId)` called once | N/A |
46	| Already saved | Tap a `saved` bubble | No-op — no new call, no state change | N/A |
47	| No serverId yet | Tap bookmark before `message_created` SSE event set `serverId` | No-op — same guard shape as `retryMessage` | N/A |
48	| Save fails | `create()` resolves `Left(Failure)` | Bubble flips to `error` (red warning); rest of session (composer, other bubbles, scroll) unaffected | Tapping `error` re-attempts the same save, returning to `saving` |
49	| Side-effect throws | `action()` inside `isolatedSideEffect` throws synchronously or async | Caught, mapped to `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, never propagates to caller | Bubble flips to `error`, same as above |
50	| Second tap while saving | Tap bookmark again while a save is already in flight for that message | No-op (re-entrancy guard, mirrors `_isSending`-style check scoped to that message) | N/A |
51	
52	</frozen-after-approval>
53	
54	## Code Map
55	
56	- `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart` -- replace `UnimplementedError` stub: `try { return right(await action()); } catch (e) { return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.toString())); }` (mirrors `entries_repository_impl.dart:46-50`'s existing catch-to-`malformedResponse` convention).
57	- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart:18-22` -- add optional `String? chatMessageId` to `create()`.
58	- `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:32-53` -- thread it to the remote data source call.
59	- `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:21-33` -- add `'chatMessageId': ?chatMessageId` to the `entries-create` body (mirrors existing `?mediaDurationSeconds`).
60	- `lib/features/entries/domain/usecases/save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart` (new) -- the shared interface/use case AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires: abstract `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` with `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> call({required String content, required String chatMessageId})`, impl `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCaseImpl(EntriesRepository repository)` forwarding to `repository.create(content: content, source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: chatMessageId)`. Port+impl in one file, pure domain (no `package:flutter`/`data` import), mirrors `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart`'s own structural convention. Deliberately narrow (just `content`/`chatMessageId`) rather than exposing `create()`'s full signature — this is the one caller that only ever needs `source: EntrySource.chat`.
61	- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` as a `lazySingleton` wrapping `sl<EntriesRepository>()`, mirroring `PendingEntryWriteTracker`'s own registration right above `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s.
62	- `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart` (new) -- sealed `BookmarkState`, `const factory` `idle()`/`saving()`/`saved()`/`error(Failure)`, mirrors `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart:13-21`.
63	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:121-193` (`ChatUiMessage`) -- add `BookmarkState bookmarkState` (default `.idle()`), extend `copyWith`/`==`/`hashCode`/`toString`.
64	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:18` (ctor) -- add `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` param (import `entries/domain/usecases/save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart` only — never `entries/domain/repositories/`).
65	- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` (new, near `retryMessage`) -- `bookmarkMessage(String messageId)`: guard `current is! title: 'Story 6.4 — Bookmark a Chat Message into an Entry'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-06'

context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** A user's own reflective Chat Message can't become a journal Entry without retyping it — `ChatUiMessage` has no bookmark affordance, `EntriesRepository.create()` has no `chatMessageId` slot even though `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already reserve it, and `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` is still an `UnimplementedError` stub explicitly waiting for this story.

**Approach:** Add a four-state (`idle`/`saving`/`saved`/`error`) bookmark button to user-only chat bubbles. `ChatCubit.bookmarkMessage(messageId)` calls the real `isolatedSideEffect` (replacing the stub) wrapping a call to a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — the shared interface AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires — which itself wraps `EntriesRepository.create(..., source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: ...)`. `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under `entries/data`/`entries/presentation`.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Bookmark affordance: `ChatMessageRole.user` bubbles only.
- `ChatCubit` depends on `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) — never `EntriesRepository` directly, never `entries/data/` or `entries/presentation/` (AGENTS.md: "RF10 must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly").
- Save runs through `isolatedSideEffect` (real body, replacing the `UnimplementedError` stub), awaited before bookmark state updates.
- Tapping `saved` is a client-side no-op; repeat backend calls for the same `chatMessageId` are themselves idempotent (200, not 409 — `openapi.yaml`'s `entries.create` doc) so no extra client dedup needed.
- A save failure never freezes the session: only the tapped bubble's state flips to `error` (retryable); composer/history/other bubbles unaffected.
- Icon + color together, never color alone: `idle` outline, `saving` spinner (static label under Reduce Motion), `saved` ochre check (`colorAccent`, `0xFFC98A3E`), `error` red warning (`colorError`). Tap target ≥44pt, `Semantics(button: true)`.
- Bookmarking requires a non-null `serverId` (the id sent as `chatMessageId`); tapping before that is a no-op, mirroring `retryMessage`'s guard.
- Both of `bookmarkMessage`'s `emit()` calls (before and after the `isolatedSideEffect` await) check `isClosed` first — not just the one after the await.
- A bookmark glyph's Reduce-Motion static label sits in a width-capped slot (e.g. wrapped the same way `bubbleContainer` is `Flexible`-constrained), so it cannot squeeze the message bubble under large accessibility text scaling.

**Ask First:** none — `chatMessageId` on `create()` is a pre-reserved slot (`Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` already exist for this story), not a new architectural call.

**Never:**
- Never import `EntriesRepository`, `entries/data/`, or `entries/presentation/` from `chat/` — only `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`.
- Never route the bookmark save through `PendingEntryWriteTracker` — its `create()` clears *any* app-wide failed pending-write on each call (written for exactly one capture flow in flight at a time), so a concurrent chat bookmark could silently clear an unrelated capture flow's visible error card.
- Never persist bookmark state across restarts — in-memory only; a stale `idle` post-reload is harmless given backend idempotency.
- Never let a bookmark failure disable the composer or affect other bubbles.
- Never introduce a second Entry model or bypass `EntriesRepository` (the use case's own only caller).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Happy path | Tap bookmark on a user bubble with `serverId` set, `idle` | Bubble flips `idle` → `saving` → `saved` (ochre check); `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase(content, chatMessageId: serverId)` called once | N/A |
| Already saved | Tap a `saved` bubble | No-op — no new call, no state change | N/A |
| No serverId yet | Tap bookmark before `message_created` SSE event set `serverId` | No-op — same guard shape as `retryMessage` | N/A |
| Save fails | `create()` resolves `Left(Failure)` | Bubble flips to `error` (red warning); rest of session (composer, other bubbles, scroll) unaffected | Tapping `error` re-attempts the same save, returning to `saving` |
| Side-effect throws | `action()` inside `isolatedSideEffect` throws synchronously or async | Caught, mapped to `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`, never propagates to caller | Bubble flips to `error`, same as above |
| Second tap while saving | Tap bookmark again while a save is already in flight for that message | No-op (re-entrancy guard, mirrors `_isSending`-style check scoped to that message) | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart` -- replace `UnimplementedError` stub: `try { return right(await action()); } catch (e) { return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: e.toString())); }` (mirrors `entries_repository_impl.dart:46-50`'s existing catch-to-`malformedResponse` convention).
- `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart:18-22` -- add optional `String? chatMessageId` to `create()`.
- `lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:32-53` -- thread it to the remote data source call.
- `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:21-33` -- add `'chatMessageId': ?chatMessageId` to the `entries-create` body (mirrors existing `?mediaDurationSeconds`).
- `lib/features/entries/domain/usecases/save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart` (new) -- the shared interface/use case AGENTS.md's RF10 rule requires: abstract `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` with `Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> call({required String content, required String chatMessageId})`, impl `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCaseImpl(EntriesRepository repository)` forwarding to `repository.create(content: content, source: EntrySource.chat, chatMessageId: chatMessageId)`. Port+impl in one file, pure domain (no `package:flutter`/`data` import), mirrors `pending_entry_write_tracker.dart`'s own structural convention. Deliberately narrow (just `content`/`chatMessageId`) rather than exposing `create()`'s full signature — this is the one caller that only ever needs `source: EntrySource.chat`.
- `lib/features/entries/entries_injection.dart` -- register `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` as a `lazySingleton` wrapping `sl<EntriesRepository>()`, mirroring `PendingEntryWriteTracker`'s own registration right above `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s.
- `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart` (new) -- sealed `BookmarkState`, `const factory` `idle()`/`saving()`/`saved()`/`error(Failure)`, mirrors `entries/domain/entities/sync_badge_state.dart:13-21`.
- `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart:121-193` (`ChatUiMessage`) -- add `BookmarkState bookmarkState` (default `.idle()`), extend `copyWith`/`==`/`hashCode`/`toString`.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:** (file path -- action; rationale is in the Code Map above)
- [x] `core/isolated_side_effect.dart` -- implement the real never-throws body.
- [x] `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart`, `data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart`, `data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- add `chatMessageId` through all three layers.

- [x] `chat/chat_injection.dart` -- wire `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` into `ChatCubit`.
- [x] `chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble.dart`, `presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` -- bookmark button UI + wiring.
- [x] `core/design_tokens.dart` -- standalone `chatBookmarkIconSize`.
- [x] Extend/add the test files listed in the Code Map per the I/O matrix, including `chat_screen_test.dart`'s new wiring test and `main_test.dart`'s fake swap.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given one of my own Chat Messages (never an AI response), when I tap the bookmark affordance, then it creates an Entry (`source=chat`, carrying `chatMessageId`) through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` only — `ChatCubit` never imports `EntriesRepository` or anything under entries' data/presentation layers.
- Given the save executes, when it runs, then it goes through the real (non-stub) `isolatedSideEffect` helper, awaited before the button's state updates.
- Given a message already in `saved`, when I tap it again, then it is a no-op — no duplicate Entry, no error surfaced.
- Given a save fails, when the error state shows, then the surrounding Chat Session remains fully usable and the button resets to a retryable `error` state rather than freezing, with state carried by icon + color together.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Decision] Bookmark save outcome silently dropped on session switch — `bookmarkMessage()` awaits `isolatedSideEffect` then re-reads `state` and rebuilds `messages` by id; `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` (`chat_cubit.dart:206-300`) replace `ChatReady.messages` wholesale and only cancel the send/retry stream (`_cancelInFlightSend`) — never a bookmark save in flight. If the user switches sessions (or starts a new one) while a save is pending, the eventual `saved`/`error` result finds no matching message in the new `ChatReady.messages` and is silently discarded: no confirmation, no error, no retryable state surfaced. **Resolved:** tracked the save's outcome in a new `_bookmarkStateByServerId` map on `ChatCubit`, keyed by the message's `serverId` (stable across a reload, unlike the in-session local `id`) — same in-memory-only, survives-session-switches lifetime as the existing `_scrollOffsets` map. `_fromDomain` applies any recorded override when a session's history (re)loads, so re-entering a session that carries the bookmarked message picks the outcome back up instead of losing it; the live emit at the end of `bookmarkMessage()` now also matches by `serverId` rather than the possibly-stale local `id`. Chose this over blocking session switches (a new UX constraint the spec never asked for) since it fixes the gap without adding one. New regression test: `test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart` ("review fix (round 2): a save that resolves after the user has switched sessions..."). [`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:592-624`]
- [x] [Review][Patch] No test for `bookmarkMessage()`'s pre-save `isClosed`/non-`ChatReady` guards or cross-message concurrency — only the `isClosed` guard *after* the `isolatedSideEffect` await is tested; the guard before the first `saving` emit, the `current is! ChatReady` early-return, and two independent messages bookmarked concurrently without cross-talk are all unexercised. **Fixed:** added all three cases to `chat_cubit_test.dart`'s `bookmarkMessage()` group. [`test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart`]
- [x] [Review][Patch] `bookmarkMessage()` tests index `messages[0]`/`messages[1]` directly, reintroducing fragility a nearby helper explicitly avoids — `sendAndCompleteWithServerId`'s own comment says it filters by role "so this helper keeps working if message ordering ever changes... instead of silently asserting on the wrong bubble," but the surrounding assertions in the same group use raw indices instead. **Reassessed, no change needed:** every existing assertion in the group has exactly one user message on screen at that point (same single-round-trip convention the `sendMessage()`/`retryMessage()` groups already use elsewhere in this file without any role-filter helper at all), so the index is never actually ambiguous there — the helper's role-filter exists for the id-lookup-after-a-round-trip use case specifically, not as a group-wide convention this violates. The one place it would have mattered (two user messages on screen at once) is the new concurrency test added above, which looks its second message up by content instead of by index or by the role-only helper (confirmed necessary: the helper always returns the *first* user message, which the new concurrency test initially tripped over before this fix).
- [x] [Review][Patch] New `chat_screen_test.dart` wiring test uses unscoped global icon finders — `find.byIcon(Icons.bookmark_border)`/`find.byIcon(Icons.check)` search the entire pumped `ChatScreen` tree rather than being scoped to the tapped bubble/button, so the test would start matching an unrelated icon elsewhere on screen if one is ever added. **Fixed:** both scoped via `find.descendant(of: find.byType(ChatBubble), matching: ...)`. [`test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart`]
- [x] [Review][Patch] Throwing `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` fake duplicated across 5 test files instead of factored into `test/support/` — a near-identical "never expected to be called" fake is hand-rolled independently in `main_test.dart`, `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `chat_cubit_test.dart`, and `chat_screen_test.dart`, instead of a shared helper (where `fake_connectivity_watcher.dart` already lives). **Fixed:** extracted the 3 byte-identical "never called" copies (`main_test.dart`, `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`) into `test/support/unused_save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart`. Left `chat_cubit_test.dart`'s and `chat_screen_test.dart`'s own fakes as-is — they're genuinely different shapes (completer-based vs. fixed-result) serving different test needs, not duplicates of this one or each other. [`test/support/unused_save_chat_message_as_entry_use_case.dart`]

## Spec Change Log

- **Round 1 review finding (intent_gap):** The original frozen Boundaries said "`ChatCubit` depends on `EntriesRepository` from `entries/domain/repositories/` only" — implemented faithfully, but that directly violates AGENTS.md's explicit RF10 rule ("must call the entries feature through a shared interface/use case, never by importing the entries repository or data source directly — doing so also violates RNF06"). Root cause was inside the frozen block, so this is an intent_gap, not a patch.
  **Amended:** `ChatCubit` now depends on a new `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` (`entries/domain/usecases/`) instead of `EntriesRepository` directly; `EntriesRepository`/`entries/data`/`entries/presentation` imports from `chat/` are now explicitly forbidden in Boundaries.
  **Known-bad state avoided:** a cross-feature import the project's own instructions name by story number (RF10) as forbidden, which would also have made every future review of this story flag the same violation.
  **Also folded in** (surfaced by the same review round, cheap to fix alongside the use-case change since the touched files are being re-derived anyway): both `bookmarkMessage()` emits now need an `isClosed` guard, not just the second one; the Reduce-Motion label needs a width-capped slot; `chatBookmarkIconSize` should be its own literal, not an alias of an unrelated token; `chat_screen_test.dart` needs a real end-to-end tap test for the `onBookmark` wiring (previously only `ChatBubble`/`ChatCubit` were tested in isolation); `test/main_test.dart` should use a throwing fake like every other touched test file, not the real DI-resolved dependency; the `pending_entry_write_tracker_test.dart` fake's new param line had a stray 2-space indent.
  **KEEP (verified correct, must survive re-derivation):** the `BookmarkState` sealed-class shape and its placement in `chat/domain/entities/`; `ChatUiMessage.bookmarkState`'s default-idle/`copyWith` extension; the `chatMessageId` threading through `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` → `data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` → `data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` (unaffected by this amendment — the use case sits *above* this, not instead of it); `isolatedSideEffect`'s real catch-to-`malformedResponse` body; `bookmarkMessage()`'s guard chain (role/serverId/already-saved/already-saving) and its `Either`-flattening from `isolatedSideEffect`; the `ChatBubble` icon/color-per-state mapping and 44pt tap target; every I/O-matrix-covering test case already written for `chat_cubit_test.dart`/`chat_bubble_test.dart` (only their `EntriesRepository` fake swaps for a `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` fake — the test *logic* is unchanged).

## Design Notes

- `BookmarkState` lives in `chat/domain/entities/`, mirroring `SyncBadgeState`'s per-feature placement — promote only if a second feature needs it.
- `chatMessageId` sent is `ChatUiMessage.serverId`, never the local UI `id` — same distinction story 6.3 established for `retryMessage`.
- No persisted bookmark flag: reload-then-re-tap is harmless given backend idempotency — simpler than threading a new field through the Hive message cache for no behavioral gain.
- `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase` is deliberately narrower than `EntriesRepository.create()` (just `content`/`chatMessageId`, `source` is implicit) — it exists only to satisfy AGENTS.md's RF10 boundary, not to become a general-purpose entries port; a future caller needing more of `create()`'s surface gets its own use case rather than this one growing extra optional params.

Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows: ## 1. `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart` (800 lines, full file read) - Constructor (L22-45): `ChatCubit(this._repository, this._connectivityWatcher, this._saveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase) : super(const ChatBootstrapLoading())`. DI pattern (see §4): `sl.registerLazySingleton(() => ChatCubit(sl(), sl(), sl()), dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close())`. Long-lived singleton — survives screen revisits within the app session. - Fields relevant to a timer-driven feature: `StreamSubscription? _connectivitySubscription` (L55), `StreamSubscription>? _sendSubscription` (L57), `Completer? _sendCompleter` (L64), `bool _isSending` (L81), `Future? _initFuture` (L88), `bool _isOffline` (L98), `final Map _scrollOffsets` (L106, in-memory, keyed by sessionId, never Hive), `final Map _bookmarkStateByServerId` (L118, in-memory, keyed by serverId). - **No `Timer`/`Timer.periodic` usage anywhere in `ChatCubit` today.** Whole-repo grep for `Timer(` / `Timer.periodic`: - `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart:28` — `Timer(_threshold, ...)` - `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:252` — `Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 1), (_) {...})` (closest precedent for a cubit-owned repeating/cancelable timer; started at L249 `_startElapsedTimer()`) - `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/entries_search_cubit.dart:86` — debounce `Timer(_debounceDuration, ...)` - `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:101,116,146` — skeleton-threshold timers (widget-State-owned, not cubit) - `lib/features/vault/presentation/widgets/pin_keypad.dart:72` - None of these live in `chat/`. A 2-minute inactivity timer for story 6.5 has no existing chat-specific precedent to reuse verbatim; `audio_entry_cubit.dart`'s `Timer.periodic` pattern (store as a field, cancel in `close()`/a stop method) is the closest cubit-lifecycle model. - `sendMessage` (L354-392) / `retryMessage` (L416-469): both guard `current is! ChatReady`, `_isSending || current.isOffline` → no-op return; both funnel into shared `_consumeStream` (L478-525), which guards `isClosed` before every `emit`, cancels prior `_sendSubscription`, and resolves via a `Completer`. - `isClosed` guard pattern used consistently before every `emit` call throughout (`_bootstrap`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `_applyStreamEvent`, `_markFailed`, `_finishSending`, `_handleConnectivityChange`, `bookmarkMessage`). - `bookmarkMessage` (L637-732) — the exact `isolatedSideEffect` call site (L675-680): ```dart final sideEffectResult = await isolatedSideEffect( () => _saveChatMessageAsEntry(content: message.content, chatMessageId: serverId), ); ``` **Awaited**, not fire-and-forget, despite `isolated_side_effect.dart`'s own doc at L9 saying "spec-6-5 reuses it fire-and-forget (unawaited)" — 6.4 awaits it so the bookmark icon can flip to saved/error; 6.5 is flagged in that same doc comment as the first unawaited caller. After resolving, result is matched (L687-695) flattening the outer isolatedSideEffect `Either` with the inner use-case `Either`, written to `_bookmarkStateByServerId` unconditionally (even if session has moved on, L701), then only applied to live state if `isClosed` is false, `state is ChatReady`, and the message is `stillVisible` by `serverId` (L703-731). - `close()` (L789-798) cancels `_connectivitySubscription`, `_sendSubscription`, completes any pending `_sendCompleter`. ## 2. `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` (full file, 215 lines) - `sealed class ChatState` (L11) → `ChatBootstrapLoading`, `ChatBootstrapError(failure)`, `ChatReady`. - `ChatReady` (L42-113): constructor fields `sessionId`, `messages` (`List`, append-only), `sessions` (`List`), `isSending = false`, `restoreScrollOffset`, `isOffline = false`. `copyWith` (L99-112) takes optional overrides for all 5 mutable fields, always reconstructs via the main constructor (no field is "sticky-default", every call must explicitly carry forward anything not being changed via `??`). - **Model for appending an Insight overlay**: story 6.4 did NOT add a new field to `ChatReady` itself — it extended `ChatUiMessage` with `bookmarkState` (default `const BookmarkState.idle()`, L130/169). Per the story-6.5 architecture decision ("layered onto 6.1's state, never a second `Resource`"), the natural analogous move is interleaving Insight entries as additional *items* in `ChatReady.messages` (i.e., a sealed `ChatListItem`/discriminated variant that `ChatUiMessage` becomes one case of, or a parallel-shaped value unioned into the same list) — consistent with how `ChatScreen`'s `ListView.builder` iterates `messages[index]` directly (see §9). The prototype's own data model confirms this: `role: 'insight'` is just another entry in the same `messages` array (see §11), not a separate collection. - `ChatUiMessage` (L122-214): fields `id`, `role` (`ChatMessageRole`), `content`, `status` (`ChatMessageStatus`), `serverId`, `createdAt`, `bookmarkState` (default `BookmarkState.idle()`). Plain class, manual `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`, `copyWith` only exposes `content`/`status`/`serverId`/`bookmarkState` (not `role`/`id`/`createdAt` — those are immutable post-construction). ## 3. `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart` (full file, 29 lines) ```dart typedef IsolatedSideEffect = Future> Function( Future Function() action, ); Future> isolatedSideEffect( Future Function() action, ) async { try { return right(await action()); } catch (error) { return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString())); } } ``` Doc comment (L9) explicitly anticipates story 6.5: "spec-6-5 reuses it fire-and-forget (unawaited)." Never throws; any sync/async exception from `action` maps to `Failure.malformedResponse`. Plain top-level function, not a class — call as `isolatedSideEffect(() => someRepoCall(...))`, discard/log the `Either` without awaiting for true fire-and-forget (today's only caller, `bookmarkMessage`, awaits it — 6.5 would be the first to NOT await). ## 4. `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart` (full file, 83 lines) - `registerChatFeature()` (L26-82): opens 2 Hive boxes (`chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) via named-instance `Box` singletons; registers `ChatRemoteDataSource` (lazySingleton, wraps `ApiClient`), `ChatRepository → ChatRepositoryImpl` (lazySingleton), `Connectivity`/`ConnectivityWatcher` (lazySingleton), and `ChatCubit` (lazySingleton, `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()`). - To add an insight use case/repository method: extend `ChatRepository`'s interface + `ChatRepositoryImpl` (no new DI registration needed, same singleton); if a dedicated use-case class is introduced (mirroring RF10's `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`), register it here as its own `sl.registerLazySingleton<...>()` line before the `ChatCubit` registration, then add it as a 4th constructor arg to `ChatCubit(...)`. ## 5. `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` — insight operation (L1307-1408) - Path `/chat/sessions/{id}/insight`, `operationId: chat.insight.create`, `x-cerne-function: chat-insight-create`, `security: [{bearerAuth: []}]` (user token, not the 3-exception anon-bearer operations). - Summary (L1310): "Generate insight — never an HTTP error; a failure becomes status='failed' (RF08)." - Path param: `id` (session id), path. - Request body (required): `{ triggerType: enum[message_count, inactivity], triggerKey: string (minLength 1) }` — both required. - Response 200 `data` object: `id` (uuid), `sessionId` (uuid), `triggerType` (same enum), `triggerKey` (string), `status: enum[generating, ready, failed, dismissed]`, `content` (string, nullable), `errorCode` (nullable, one of the 13-code taxonomy), `dismissedAt` (nullable date-time), `createdAt` (date-time). All of these listed fields are `required` in the schema (including `content`/`errorCode`/`dismissedAt` being present-but-nullable). - Real call URL per AGENTS.md convention: `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/chat-insight-create/`. - No explicit per-call error-code subset documented beyond the global 13-code taxonomy; the operation's own note says failures surface as `status='failed'` in a 200 response, not as an HTTP error — i.e. this endpoint is designed to always return 200 with the Insight object carrying its own `status`, not propagate a `Left(Failure)` the way `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` do. (Still wrap the actual network call in the normal `Either` pattern for transport-level failures — offline/timeout/auth — separate from the in-payload `status='failed'`.) ## 6. `docs/input/backend/README.md` + error/known-bugs docs - `docs/input/backend/README.md:39`: `| POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight | chat-insight-create |` — confirms the function-name mapping. - No insight-specific entries in `docs/input/backend/known-bugs.md` or `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md` (grep returned nothing). - `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` (full file, 26 lines): closed 13-code list, each with HTTP status + retryable flag. Relevant for this story: `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` (504, retryable) is the most likely insight-generation failure code; `NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP response at all. No code is insight-exclusive — all 13 are shared across endpoints. - `docs/input/requirements.md:346`: `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` doc note explicitly names "chat/insight/summary/dashboard" as the 4 endpoints that can produce it. ## 7. `lib/features/chat/domain/` — full listing ``` lib/features/chat/domain/.gitkeep lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart (abstract ChatRepository — see below) lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart ``` No insight-related entity/method exists yet. `ChatRepository` (full file read, 73 lines) has exactly 4 methods: `listSessions`, `createSession`, `listMessages`, `sendMessage` (stream), `retryMessage` (stream) — **no insight method stub**; one must be added, e.g. `Future> generateInsight(String sessionId, {required String triggerType, required String triggerKey})`. `ChatSession` entity (full file read) already carries `userMessageCount` (int) and `lastUserMessageAt` (String?) fields from the backend — these are session-lifetime totals (not "since last insight window"), so they likely cannot be reused as-is for the "5 messages since last insight" trigger; a separate client-side per-session counter (mirroring `_bookmarkStateByServerId`'s in-memory-map pattern) is probably needed on `ChatCubit`. `ChatStreamEvent` (full file read) is a plain sealed class (not freezed) with 3 members — a new `Insight` entity should likely follow this same plain-sealed-class convention (or `BookmarkState`'s `const factory` constructor pattern, §12) rather than introducing `freezed` for a new chat type. ## 8. `lib/features/chat/data/` — full listing ``` lib/features/chat/data/.gitkeep lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart (full file read — see below) lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart (full file read — see below) lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_session_dto.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_session_dto.g.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_message_dto.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_message_dto.g.dart lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart ``` `ChatRemoteDataSource` calls non-streaming endpoints via `_apiClient.get`/`_apiClient.post` with `pathParams: [...]` appended as trailing path segments (e.g. L82-85 `_apiClient.get('chat-messages-list', pathParams: [sessionId])`) — an insight call would be `_apiClient.post('chat-insight-create', pathParams: [sessionId], data: {...})`, parsed via a new `InsightDto.fromJson`. `ChatRepositoryImpl` wraps each datasource call, with "persist then return" Hive-caching for `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` only; `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` are pure passthroughs with **no Hive persistence** (Design Notes quoted at L120-121: "Chat holds no local write queue"). An insight method would most naturally be a pure passthrough too (no new Hive box), consistent with §14 below. ## 9. `chat_bubble.dart` + `chat_screen.dart` (both full files read) - `chat_screen.dart` L191-211: the message list is `ChatReady(messages: final messages) => ListView.builder(..., itemCount: messages.length, itemBuilder: (context, index) => ChatBubble(key: ValueKey(messages[index].id), message: messages[index], onRetry: ..., onBookmark: ...))`. Long-lived singleton — survives screen revisits within the app session. - Fields relevant to a timer-driven feature: `StreamSubscription? _connectivitySubscription` (L55), `StreamSubscription>? _sendSubscription` (L57), `Completer? _sendCompleter` (L64), `bool _isSending` (L81), `Future? _initFuture` (L88), `bool _isOffline` (L98), `final Map _scrollOffsets` (L106, in-memory, keyed by sessionId, never Hive), `final Map _bookmarkStateByServerId` (L118, in-memory, keyed by serverId). - **No `Timer`/`Timer.periodic` usage anywhere in `ChatCubit` today.** Whole-repo grep for `Timer(` / `Timer.periodic`: - `lib/core/navigation/placeholder_screens.dart:28` — `Timer(_threshold, ...)` - `lib/features/capture/presentation/cubit/audio_entry_cubit.dart:252` — `Timer.periodic(const Duration(seconds: 1), (_) {...})` (closest precedent for a cubit-owned repeating/cancelable timer; started at L249 `_startElapsedTimer()`) - `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/entries_search_cubit.dart:86` — debounce `Timer(_debounceDuration, ...)` - `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:101,116,146` — skeleton-threshold timers (widget-State-owned, not cubit) - `lib/features/vault/presentation/widgets/pin_keypad.dart:72` - None of these live in `chat/`. A 2-minute inactivity timer for story 6.5 has no existing chat-specific precedent to reuse verbatim; `audio_entry_cubit.dart`'s `Timer.periodic` pattern (store as a field, cancel in `close()`/a stop method) is the closest cubit-lifecycle model. - `sendMessage` (L354-392) / `retryMessage` (L416-469): both guard `current is! ChatReady`, `_isSending || current.isOffline` → no-op return; both funnel into shared `_consumeStream` (L478-525), which guards `isClosed` before every `emit`, cancels prior `_sendSubscription`, and resolves via a `Completer`. - `isClosed` guard pattern used consistently before every `emit` call throughout (`_bootstrap`, `switchSession`, `startNewSession`, `_applyStreamEvent`, `_markFailed`, `_finishSending`, `_handleConnectivityChange`, `bookmarkMessage`). - `bookmarkMessage` (L637-732) — the exact `isolatedSideEffect` call site (L675-680): ```dart final sideEffectResult = await isolatedSideEffect( () => _saveChatMessageAsEntry(content: message.content, chatMessageId: serverId), ); ``` **Awaited**, not fire-and-forget, despite `isolated_side_effect.dart`'s own doc at L9 saying "spec-6-5 reuses it fire-and-forget (unawaited)" — 6.4 awaits it so the bookmark icon can flip to saved/error; 6.5 is flagged in that same doc comment as the first unawaited caller. After resolving, result is matched (L687-695) flattening the outer isolatedSideEffect `Either` with the inner use-case `Either`, written to `_bookmarkStateByServerId` unconditionally (even if session has moved on, L701), then only applied to live state if `isClosed` is false, `state is ChatReady`, and the message is `stillVisible` by `serverId` (L703-731). - `close()` (L789-798) cancels `_connectivitySubscription`, `_sendSubscription`, completes any pending `_sendCompleter`. ## 2. `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_state.dart` (full file, 215 lines) - `sealed class ChatState` (L11) → `ChatBootstrapLoading`, `ChatBootstrapError(failure)`, `ChatReady`. - `ChatReady` (L42-113): constructor fields `sessionId`, `messages` (`List`, append-only), `sessions` (`List`), `isSending = false`, `restoreScrollOffset`, `isOffline = false`. `copyWith` (L99-112) takes optional overrides for all 5 mutable fields, always reconstructs via the main constructor (no field is "sticky-default", every call must explicitly carry forward anything not being changed via `??`). - **Model for appending an Insight overlay**: story 6.4 did NOT add a new field to `ChatReady` itself — it extended `ChatUiMessage` with `bookmarkState` (default `const BookmarkState.idle()`, L130/169). Per the story-6.5 architecture decision ("layered onto 6.1's state, never a second `Resource`"), the natural analogous move is interleaving Insight entries as additional *items* in `ChatReady.messages` (i.e., a sealed `ChatListItem`/discriminated variant that `ChatUiMessage` becomes one case of, or a parallel-shaped value unioned into the same list) — consistent with how `ChatScreen`'s `ListView.builder` iterates `messages[index]` directly (see §9). The prototype's own data model confirms this: `role: 'insight'` is just another entry in the same `messages` array (see §11), not a separate collection. - `ChatUiMessage` (L122-214): fields `id`, `role` (`ChatMessageRole`), `content`, `status` (`ChatMessageStatus`), `serverId`, `createdAt`, `bookmarkState` (default `BookmarkState.idle()`). Plain class, manual `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`, `copyWith` only exposes `content`/`status`/`serverId`/`bookmarkState` (not `role`/`id`/`createdAt` — those are immutable post-construction). ## 3. `lib/core/isolated_side_effect.dart` (full file, 29 lines) ```dart typedef IsolatedSideEffect = Future> Function( Future Function() action, ); Future> isolatedSideEffect( Future Function() action, ) async { try { return right(await action()); } catch (error) { return left(Failure.malformedResponse(message: error.toString())); } } ``` Doc comment (L9) explicitly anticipates story 6.5: "spec-6-5 reuses it fire-and-forget (unawaited)." Never throws; any sync/async exception from `action` maps to `Failure.malformedResponse`. Plain top-level function, not a class — call as `isolatedSideEffect(() => someRepoCall(...))`, discard/log the `Either` without awaiting for true fire-and-forget (today's only caller, `bookmarkMessage`, awaits it — 6.5 would be the first to NOT await). ## 4. `lib/features/chat/chat_injection.dart` (full file, 83 lines) - `registerChatFeature()` (L26-82): opens 2 Hive boxes (`chat_sessions`, `chat_messages`) via named-instance `Box` singletons; registers `ChatRemoteDataSource` (lazySingleton, wraps `ApiClient`), `ChatRepository → ChatRepositoryImpl` (lazySingleton), `Connectivity`/`ConnectivityWatcher` (lazySingleton), and `ChatCubit` (lazySingleton, `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()`). - To add an insight use case/repository method: extend `ChatRepository`'s interface + `ChatRepositoryImpl` (no new DI registration needed, same singleton); if a dedicated use-case class is introduced (mirroring RF10's `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`), register it here as its own `sl.registerLazySingleton<...>()` line before the `ChatCubit` registration, then add it as a 4th constructor arg to `ChatCubit(...)`. ## 5. `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` — insight operation (L1307-1408) - Path `/chat/sessions/{id}/insight`, `operationId: chat.insight.create`, `x-cerne-function: chat-insight-create`, `security: [{bearerAuth: []}]` (user token, not the 3-exception anon-bearer operations). - Summary (L1310): "Generate insight — never an HTTP error; a failure becomes status='failed' (RF08)." - Path param: `id` (session id), path. - Request body (required): `{ triggerType: enum[message_count, inactivity], triggerKey: string (minLength 1) }` — both required. - Response 200 `data` object: `id` (uuid), `sessionId` (uuid), `triggerType` (same enum), `triggerKey` (string), `status: enum[generating, ready, failed, dismissed]`, `content` (string, nullable), `errorCode` (nullable, one of the 13-code taxonomy), `dismissedAt` (nullable date-time), `createdAt` (date-time). All of these listed fields are `required` in the schema (including `content`/`errorCode`/`dismissedAt` being present-but-nullable). - Real call URL per AGENTS.md convention: `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/chat-insight-create/`. - No explicit per-call error-code subset documented beyond the global 13-code taxonomy; the operation's own note says failures surface as `status='failed'` in a 200 response, not as an HTTP error — i.e. this endpoint is designed to always return 200 with the Insight object carrying its own `status`, not propagate a `Left(Failure)` the way `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` do. (Still wrap the actual network call in the normal `Either` pattern for transport-level failures — offline/timeout/auth — separate from the in-payload `status='failed'`.) ## 6. `docs/input/backend/README.md` + error/known-bugs docs - `docs/input/backend/README.md:39`: `| POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight | chat-insight-create |` — confirms the function-name mapping. - No insight-specific entries in `docs/input/backend/known-bugs.md` or `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md` (grep returned nothing). - `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md` (full file, 26 lines): closed 13-code list, each with HTTP status + retryable flag. Relevant for this story: `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` (504, retryable) is the most likely insight-generation failure code; `NETWORK_OFFLINE` has no HTTP response at all. No code is insight-exclusive — all 13 are shared across endpoints. - `docs/input/requirements.md:346`: `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` doc note explicitly names "chat/insight/summary/dashboard" as the 4 endpoints that can produce it. ## 7. `lib/features/chat/domain/` — full listing ``` lib/features/chat/domain/.gitkeep lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart (abstract ChatRepository — see below) lib/features/chat/domain/services/connectivity_watcher.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_message.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_stream_event.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_session.dart ``` No insight-related entity/method exists yet. `ChatRepository` (full file read, 73 lines) has exactly 4 methods: `listSessions`, `createSession`, `listMessages`, `sendMessage` (stream), `retryMessage` (stream) — **no insight method stub**; one must be added, e.g. `Future> generateInsight(String sessionId, {required String triggerType, required String triggerKey})`. `ChatSession` entity (full file read) already carries `userMessageCount` (int) and `lastUserMessageAt` (String?) fields from the backend — these are session-lifetime totals (not "since last insight window"), so they likely cannot be reused as-is for the "5 messages since last insight" trigger; a separate client-side per-session counter (mirroring `_bookmarkStateByServerId`'s in-memory-map pattern) is probably needed on `ChatCubit`. `ChatStreamEvent` (full file read) is a plain sealed class (not freezed) with 3 members — a new `Insight` entity should likely follow this same plain-sealed-class convention (or `BookmarkState`'s `const factory` constructor pattern, §12) rather than introducing `freezed` for a new chat type. ## 8. `lib/features/chat/data/` — full listing ``` lib/features/chat/data/.gitkeep lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart (full file read — see below) lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart (full file read — see below) lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_session_dto.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_session_dto.g.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_message_dto.dart lib/features/chat/data/models/chat_message_dto.g.dart lib/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher.dart ``` `ChatRemoteDataSource` calls non-streaming endpoints via `_apiClient.get`/`_apiClient.post` with `pathParams: [...]` appended as trailing path segments (e.g. L82-85 `_apiClient.get('chat-messages-list', pathParams: [sessionId])`) — an insight call would be `_apiClient.post('chat-insight-create', pathParams: [sessionId], data: {...})`, parsed via a new `InsightDto.fromJson`. `ChatRepositoryImpl` wraps each datasource call, with "persist then return" Hive-caching for `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` only; `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` are pure passthroughs with **no Hive persistence** (Design Notes quoted at L120-121: "Chat holds no local write queue"). An insight method would most naturally be a pure passthrough too (no new Hive box), consistent with §14 below. ## 9. `chat_bubble.dart` + `chat_screen.dart` (both full files read) - `chat_screen.dart` L191-211: the message list is `ChatReady(messages: final messages) => ListView.builder(..., itemCount: messages.length, itemBuilder: (context, index) => ChatBubble(key: ValueKey(messages[index].id), message: messages[index], onRetry: ..., onBookmark: ...))`. To interleave an Insight card, `itemBuilder` needs a `switch`/type-check on the item at `index` (e.g. `switch (item) { ChatUiMessage m => ChatBubble(...), InsightItem i => InsightCard(...) }`) — this confirms the single-list-of-mixed-items architecture is the natural fit, not a second overlay widget positioned independently. - `onBookmark`/`onRetry` wiring pattern (L202-209): callbacks are wired unconditionally per-item; `ChatBubble` itself gates visibility internally (only user bubbles show bookmark, only failed AI bubbles show retry) — an `onDismiss` callback for the Insight card would follow the same "wire unconditionally, let the card decide whether to render the affordance" convention. - `chat_bubble.dart` bookmark icon/color pattern (L320-369, `_BookmarkIndicator`): a `StatelessWidget` taking `state` + `reduceMotion`, `switch` over the sealed state returning `Icon`/`Text` per variant, colors driven by `DesignTokens.colorAccent` (saved) / `colorError` (error) / `colorTextSecondary` (idle/saving). The bookmark button itself (L187-211, `buildBookmarkButton`) wraps in `InkWell` + `ConstrainedBox(minWidth/minHeight: DesignTokens.insertionModalTapTargetMin)` + `Semantics(button: true, label: ..., excludeSemantics: true)` gated on the callback being non-null — this exact shape (tappable glyph, 44pt min tap target, conditional Semantics wrapper) is the template for the Insight card's dismiss "x". - No existing "left-spine card" Flutter widget exists anywhere in `lib/` yet (confirmed no `kanbanCardSpineWidth`-consuming widget was read, but the token exists at `design_tokens.dart:438` for the Kanban card — not yet built in Flutter since Planos de Ação is an extension-scope placeholder per AGENTS.md). The Insight card will be the **first** left-spine card actually implemented in Flutter. ## 10. `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` — relevant tokens - `colorAccent = Color(0xFFC98A3E)` (L27, doc: "CTA, insight, saved bookmark") — the ochre spine/label color. - `colorTextSecondary = Color(0xFF6B6255)` (L48) — dismiss "x" icon color (per prototype markup, §11). - `colorTextPrimary = Color(0xFF241F19)` (L45) — insight body text color. - `colorSurfaceElevated = Color(0xFFFBF9F4)` (L39) — card background (matches AI bubble background). - `textMonoCaption` (L166-172): `IBMPlexMono` (`_fontMono`, L106) w500, 12/16, letterSpacing 0.2 — exact spec for the mono "INSIGHT" label per prototype (`font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.2px`, §11). - `textBodyMd` (L149-154: Karla 400, 14/20) matches the prototype's insight body text (`font-size:14px;line-height:20px`) more closely than `textBodyLg` (16/24, used for chat bubbles) — **no exact 14px/20px token pairing exists for body text at this precise line-height**; `textBodyMd` is the closest existing token (same 14/20 metrics) and should be reused rather than adding a new one. - `elevation1` (L217-223) matches the prototype's `box-shadow:0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` for the insight card. - `radiusMd = 16` (L204) matches the card's `border-radius:16px`. - No existing "spine width" token — `kanbanCardSpineWidth = 3` (L438) is the only precedent (3px), but the prototype's actual Home/Chat insight-card markup uses the same `width:3px` (see §11) — reusable as-is, or a new `chatInsightSpineWidth` alias could be declared equal to it per RNF08 (every visual literal must be a named token). - No token yet exists for: the card's own internal padding (prototype: `padding:14px 16px 14px 20px`, none of 14/16/20 individually land exactly on existing `EdgeInsets` tokens except 16=`spacingMd`), the label-row `margin-bottom:6px`, or the dismiss icon's `font-size:14px`. All of these need new named constants in `design_tokens.dart` per RNF08 before implementation (never hardcoded in the widget file). ## 11. `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` + raw HTML — Insight card visual spec - Section 2.2 (L65): "Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label 'INSIGHT', 'x' to dismiss, interleaved in the messages." - Section 3 "Spine" (L169-172): 3 spine contexts exist project-wide; context 1 is "Proactive insight in the chat — ochre" (spine width not given in the Markdown extract itself — only in raw HTML, below). - Section 6 "Component library" (L215): `Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button`. - **Exact pixel spec, from raw `cerne-prototype.html`'s own live markup** (grep'd directly since the Markdown extract omits pixel values for this component): ```html
INSIGHT
{{ msg.text }}
 ``` → spine: `width:3px` (left-aligned, full height, `#C98A3E` = `colorAccent`); card: `border-radius:16px` (`radiusMd`), `background:#FBF9F4` (`colorSurfaceElevated`), `elevation1` shadow; inner padding `14px 16px 14px 20px` (top/right/bottom/left — note the extra 2dp on the left beyond `spacingMd` to clear the spine, same convention `kanbanCardPadding` already uses for its own spine, `design_tokens.dart:630-635`); label row `margin-bottom:6px`; label text = `textMonoCaption`-equivalent (IBM Plex Mono 500 12px, letter-spacing .2, color `colorAccent`); dismiss icon = Phosphor `ph-x`, `font-size:14px`, color `#6B6255` (`colorTextSecondary`), no stated min-tap-target in the prototype (but `insertionModalTapTargetMin`=44 is the project's standing a11y floor for any tappable icon, per `ChatBubble`'s own retry/bookmark affordances — should still be applied); body text `font-size:14px;line-height:20px` Karla 400, color `#241F19` (`colorTextPrimary`). - The prototype's own React-ish demo JS also confirms the data-shape precedent: insight is just another item with `role: 'insight'` in the same `messages` array (`{ id: 5, role: 'insight', time: '09:15', text: '...' }`), with `addInsight()`/`dismissInsight(id)` mutating that same array — directly corroborating the "interleaved into the existing list, no second container" architecture decision. ## 12. `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/bookmark_state.dart` (full file, 88 lines) ```dart sealed class BookmarkState { const BookmarkState(); const factory BookmarkState.idle() = BookmarkIdle; const factory BookmarkState.saving() = BookmarkSaving; const factory BookmarkState.saved() = BookmarkSaved; const factory BookmarkState.error(Failure failure) = BookmarkError; } ``` Each variant (`BookmarkIdle`, `BookmarkSaving`, `BookmarkSaved`, `BookmarkError(failure)`) is a plain class (no `freezed`) with manual `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`. This is the exact template to mirror for any small sealed Insight-related value type (e.g. an `InsightStatus`/`InsightItem` sealed class for `generating`/`ready`/`failed`/`dismissed`, matching the backend's own `status` enum at §5). ## 13. `test/features/chat/` — filenames only ``` test/features/chat/chat_flow_e2e_test.dart test/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source_test.dart test/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart test/features/chat/data/services/connectivity_plus_watcher_test.dart test/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit_test.dart test/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen_test.dart test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/chat_bubble_test.dart ``` No existing insight-specific test file — story 6.5 will need either new test files (e.g. `chat_insight_...`) or extensions to all 6 of the above (datasource test for the new endpoint call, repository-impl test, cubit test for trigger/timer logic, screen test for interleaved rendering, plus likely a new widget test file for the Insight card itself since `chat_bubble_test.dart` is scoped to `ChatBubble` only). `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart` is the most likely home for a full trigger-to-render-to-dismiss integration scenario. ## 14. Hive/local-cache convention check Only two chat-related Hive boxes exist, both registered in `chat_injection.dart:18-19,27-28`: `chat_sessions` (`chatSessionsBoxName`) and `chat_messages` (`chatMessagesBoxName`), each a `Box`. Confirmed via `ChatRepositoryImpl` (full file, §8) that **only** `listSessions`/`createSession`/`listMessages` write through to these boxes; `sendMessage`/`retryMessage` are explicit no-cache passthroughs (Design Notes quote at L120-121: "Chat holds no local write queue for this story"). No third chat Hive box, no insight-named box anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via the `find`/`grep -l Hive` search in §8/14 overlap). This supports treating the Insight as ephemeral/in-memory only (living on `ChatReady`'s item list / `ChatCubit`'s own fields, never persisted to Hive, never reloaded from `listMessages`/`_fromDomain` on session switch) — consistent with the epic framing and with `_scrollOffsets`/`_bookmarkStateByServerId`'s own existing in-memory-map convention on `ChatCubit` (§1).

---
title: 'Story 6.5 — Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-06'
status: 'draft'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.

**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**

## Intent

**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.

**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Per active session: a client-side counter (reset to 0 on each fire) counts user messages sent via `sendMessage` only (never `retryMessage` — no new user message is actually sent); a `Timer` restarts on every `sendMessage` call and on every fire. Whichever reaches its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`; firing immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves — so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** (fire-and-forget) — the first caller to not await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await). Composer, other bubbles, and ordinary sends/retries are never blocked by it.
- A failure — transport-level `Left`, or a 200 response with `status` != `'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no error overlay, no retry affordance.
- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already construct `ChatReady` directly (not `copyWith`), so each naturally starts a session with `activeInsight: null` and a fresh trigger window — no extra reset code needed at the field level, only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those same three sites.
- `dismissInsight()` only clears `activeInsight`, via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (carrying every other current field forward) — `copyWith`'s `??` pattern cannot express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` was designed to never clear instead of fixing `copyWith`. Never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint exists in the contract; response `dismissedAt` is informational only) and never touches scroll position or any other field.
- If an insight resolves after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved the user to a different session, drop it (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches the session the call was made for).
- Insight card: ochre left spine (`colorAccent`), mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" (`colorTextSecondary`), body text (`colorTextPrimary`) — every new visual value (spine width, card padding, label-row spacing, dismiss icon size) is a named `design_tokens.dart` constant, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
- `ChatCubit`'s inactivity `Duration` is constructor-overridable (default = the real 2-minute constant) so tests can inject a short duration instead of waiting 2 real minutes.

**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight`-field shape, the counter/timer reset-before-fire ordering, and the testability seam above are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` is silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").

**Never:**
- Never call the backend on dismiss.
- Never show a card, or surface `errorCode`, for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository` — unrelated to entries.
- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box) — in-memory only, and unlike bookmark state, not even reconciled back after a session switch.

| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |
