content.content:
1	---
2	title: 'Story 6.5 — Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation'
3	type: 'feature'
4	created: '2026-11-06'
5	status: 'draft'
6	review_loop_iteration: 0
7	context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
8	---
9	
10	<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
11	
12	## Intent
13	
14	**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.
15	
16	**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.
17	
18	## Boundaries & Constraints
19	
20	**Always:**
21	- Per active session: a client-side counter (reset to 0 on each fire) counts user messages sent via `sendMessage` only (never `retryMessage` — no new user message is actually sent); a `Timer` restarts on every `sendMessage` call and on every fire. Whichever reaches its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`; firing immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves — so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
22	- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** (fire-and-forget) — the first caller to not await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await). Composer, other bubbles, and ordinary sends/retries are never blocked by it.
23	- A failure — transport-level `Left`, or a 200 response with `status` != `'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no error overlay, no retry affordance.
24	- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already construct `ChatReady` directly (not `copyWith`), so each naturally starts a session with `activeInsight: null` and a fresh trigger window — no extra reset code needed at the field level, only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those same three sites.
25	- `dismissInsight()` only clears `activeInsight`, via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (carrying every other current field forward) — `copyWith`'s `??` pattern cannot express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` was designed to never clear instead of fixing `copyWith`. Never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint exists in the contract; response `dismissedAt` is informational only) and never touches scroll position or any other field.
26	- If an insight resolves after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved the user to a different session, drop it (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches the session the call was made for).
27	- Insight card: ochre left spine (`colorAccent`), mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" (`colorTextSecondary`), body text (`colorTextPrimary`) — every new visual value (spine width, card padding, label-row spacing, dismiss icon size) is a named `design_tokens.dart` constant, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
28	- `ChatCubit`'s inactivity `Duration` is constructor-overridable (default = the real 2-minute constant) so tests can inject a short duration instead of waiting 2 real minutes.
29	
30	**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight`-field shape, the counter/timer reset-before-fire ordering, and the testability seam above are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` is silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").
31	
32	**Never:**
33	- Never call the backend on dismiss.
34	- Never show a card, or surface `errorCode`, for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
35	- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
36	- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository` — unrelated to entries.
37	- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
38	- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box) — in-memory only, and unlike bookmark state, not even reconciled back after a session switch.
39	
40	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
41	
42	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
43	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
44	| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
45	| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
46	| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
47	| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
48	| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
49	| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
50	| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |
51	
52	</frozen-after-approval>
53	
54	## Code Map
55	
56	- `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_insight.dart` (new) -- plain `ChatInsight` (`id`, `content`; manual `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`, mirrors `ChatSession`'s own shape) + `enum InsightTriggerType { messageCount, inactivity }` + an extension `wireValue` mapping to `'message_count'`/`'inactivity'` (enum names don't match the wire strings, unlike `EntrySource.name`).
57	- `lib/features/chat/domain/insight_trigger_config.dart` (new) -- top-level `const int insightMessageCountThreshold = 5;` and `const Duration defaultInsightInactivityTimeout = Duration(minutes: 2);`, mirroring `lib/features/vault/domain/vault_idle_timeout.dart`'s own standalone-constant convention.
58	- `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` -- add `Future<Either<Failure, ChatInsight?>> generateInsight(String sessionId, {required InsightTriggerType triggerType, required String triggerKey})`; `null` means "no insight to show" (any non-`ready` status), not a failure.

title: 'Story 6.5 — Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-06'
status: 'draft'

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.

**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Per active session: a client-side counter (reset to 0 on each fire) counts user messages sent via `sendMessage` only (never `retryMessage` — no new user message is actually sent); a `Timer` restarts on every `sendMessage` call and on every fire. Whichever reaches its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`; firing immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves — so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** (fire-and-forget) — the first caller to not await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await). Composer, other bubbles, and ordinary sends/retries are never blocked by it.
- A failure — transport-level `Left`, or a 200 response with `status` != `'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no error overlay, no retry affordance.
- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already construct `ChatReady` directly (not `copyWith`), so each naturally starts a session with `activeInsight: null` and a fresh trigger window — no extra reset code needed at the field level, only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those same three sites.
- `dismissInsight()` only clears `activeInsight`, via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (carrying every other current field forward) — `copyWith`'s `??` pattern cannot express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` was designed to never clear instead of fixing `copyWith`. Never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint exists in the contract; response `dismissedAt` is informational only) and never touches scroll position or any other field.
- If an insight resolves after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved the user to a different session, drop it (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches the session the call was made for).
- Insight card: ochre left spine (`colorAccent`), mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" (`colorTextSecondary`), body text (`colorTextPrimary`) — every new visual value (spine width, card padding, label-row spacing, dismiss icon size) is a named `design_tokens.dart` constant, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
- `ChatCubit`'s inactivity `Duration` is constructor-overridable (default = the real 2-minute constant) so tests can inject a short duration instead of waiting 2 real minutes.

**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight`-field shape, the counter/timer reset-before-fire ordering, and the testability seam above are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` is silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").

**Never:**
- Never call the backend on dismiss.
- Never show a card, or surface `errorCode`, for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository` — unrelated to entries.
- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box) — in-memory only, and unlike bookmark state, not even reconciled back after a session switch.

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |

| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |

**Always:**
- Per active session: a client-side counter (reset to 0 on each fire) counts user messages sent via `sendMessage` only (never `retryMessage` — no new user message is actually sent); a `Timer` restarts on every `sendMessage` call and on every fire. Whichever reaches its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`; firing immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves — so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** (fire-and-forget) — the first caller to not await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await). Composer, other bubbles, and ordinary sends/retries are never blocked by it.
- A failure — transport-level `Left`, or a 200 response with `status` != `'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no error overlay, no retry affordance.
- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already construct `ChatReady` directly (not `copyWith`), so each naturally starts a session with `activeInsight: null` and a fresh trigger window — no extra reset code needed at the field level, only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those same three sites.
- `dismissInsight()` only clears `activeInsight`, via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (carrying every other current field forward) — `copyWith`'s `??` pattern cannot express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` was designed to never clear instead of fixing `copyWith`. Never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint exists in the contract; response `dismissedAt` is informational only) and never touches scroll position or any other field.
- If an insight resolves after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved the user to a different session, drop it (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches the session the call was made for).
- Insight card: ochre left spine (`colorAccent`), mono "INSIGHT" label, dismiss "x" (`colorTextSecondary`), body text (`colorTextPrimary`) — every new visual value (spine width, card padding, label-row spacing, dismiss icon size) is a named `design_tokens.dart` constant, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
- `ChatCubit`'s inactivity `Duration` is constructor-overridable (default = the real 2-minute constant) so tests can inject a short duration instead of waiting 2 real minutes.

**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight`-field shape, the counter/timer reset-before-fire ordering, and the testability seam above are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` is silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").

**Never:**
- Never call the backend on dismiss.
- Never show a card, or surface `errorCode`, for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository` — unrelated to entries.
- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box) — in-memory only, and unlike bookmark state, not even reconciled back after a session switch.

Proceeding with **[K] Keep full spec** — this is one cohesive feature per the epic's own framing (the trigger mechanism and the card it injects are inseparable; splitting would defer half of an otherwise-worthless mechanism), consistent with AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy and `docs/input/requirements.md`'s treatment of RF08 as a single mechanism-only requirement.

**Spec:** `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-5-proactive-insight-injection-failure-isolation.md`
**Token count:** ~3,300 tokens (target 900–1600) — kept in full per the decision above; the overage is investigation density (exact file/line anchors, DTO field lists, test-extension notes), not padding, so trimming further would start cutting actionability rather than fluff.

**What it covers:**
- A per-session trigger window on `ChatCubit`: a message counter + a `Timer`, racing — whichever hits 5 user messages or 2 minutes idle first fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()`, then immediately reopens a fresh window (new key, reset counter, restarted timer) before the network call even resolves, so "never twice per window" holds structurally.
- The call is fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (6.4's helper, its first *unawaited* caller) — any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is dropped silently, no UI trace at all.

- `dismissInsight()` clears it via direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (`copyWith`'s `??` can't null out a field) — no backend call, since the frozen contract has no dismiss endpoint.
- New domain entity/config, DTO, repo method, widget, 4 design tokens, and extensions across 5 test files.

15	+---
16	+
17	+<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
18	+
19	+## Intent
20	+
21	+**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.
22	+
23	+**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.
24	+
25	+## Boundaries & Constraints
26	+
27	+**Always:**
28	+- Per active session: a counter (user messages sent via `sendMessage` only, never `retryMessage`) and a `Timer` (restarted on every `sendMessage` and every fire) race; whichever hits its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`, then immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves, so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
29	+- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** — the first caller not to await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await it).
30	+- A failure — transport `Left`, or a 200 with `status != 'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no overlay, no retry affordance.
31	+- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; the 3 existing direct `ChatReady(...)` constructions in `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already start it `null` — only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those sites.
32	+- `dismissInsight()` clears `activeInsight` via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (`copyWith`'s `??` can't express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` never clears instead of fixing `copyWith`); never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint in the contract) and never touches any other field.
33	+- An insight resolving after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved away is dropped (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches).
34	+- Insight card tokens (spine width, card padding, label spacing, dismiss icon size) go in `design_tokens.dart`, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
35	+
36	+**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight` shape, reset-before-fire ordering, and the `Duration` test seam are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").
37	+
38	+**Never:**
39	+- Never call the backend on dismiss, or show a card / surface `errorCode` for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
40	+- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
41	+- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository`.
42	+- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
43	+- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box, no cross-session reconciliation unlike bookmark state).
44	+
45	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
46	+
47	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
48	+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
49	+| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
50	+| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
51	+| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
52	+| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
53	+| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
54	+| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
55	+| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |
56	+
57	+</frozen-after-approval>

94	+**Acceptance Criteria:**
95	+- Given either 5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity within the active Chat Session, when that condition is satisfied first, then `generateInsight` is called exactly once for that window — never both, never twice.
96	+- Given the Insight card appears, when it renders, then it is interleaved into the chat stream (after the last message) as the only accent-colored element, via `ChatReady.activeInsight` — never a second state container.
97	+- Given Insight generation fails (transport or in-payload), when the failure occurs, then it is fully silent — composer stays enabled, no error overlay, ordinary chat keeps working.
98	+- Given an Insight is visible, when I dismiss it, then scroll position and all other conversation state are unaffected.

diff --git a/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-5-proactive-insight-injection-failure-isolation.md b/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-5-proactive-insight-injection-failure-isolation.md

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+---
+title: 'Story 6.5 — Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation'
+type: 'feature'
+created: '2026-11-06'
+status: 'in-review'
+review_loop_iteration: 0
+baseline_commit: '09b24965a5ca704f231b1899c7792e83f150bf87'
+context: ['{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md']
+---
+
+<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">
+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.
+
+**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Per active session: a counter (user messages sent via `sendMessage` only, never `retryMessage`) and a `Timer` (restarted on every `sendMessage` and every fire) race; whichever hits its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`, then immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves, so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
+- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** — the first caller not to await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await it).
+- A failure — transport `Left`, or a 200 with `status != 'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no overlay, no retry affordance.
+- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; the 3 existing direct `ChatReady(...)` constructions in `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already start it `null` — only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those sites.
+- `dismissInsight()` clears `activeInsight` via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (`copyWith`'s `??` can't express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` never clears instead of fixing `copyWith`); never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint in the contract) and never touches any other field.
+- An insight resolving after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved away is dropped (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches).
+- Insight card tokens (spine width, card padding, label spacing, dismiss icon size) go in `design_tokens.dart`, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
+
+**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight` shape, reset-before-fire ordering, and the `Duration` test seam are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").
+
+**Never:**
+- Never call the backend on dismiss, or show a card / surface `errorCode` for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
+- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
+- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository`.
+- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
+- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box, no cross-session reconciliation unlike bookmark state).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
+| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
+| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
+| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
+| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |
+
+</frozen-after-approval>
+
+## Code Map
+
+- `lib/features/chat/domain/entities/chat_insight.dart` (new) -- plain `ChatInsight` (`id`, `content`; manual `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`, mirrors `ChatSession`) + `enum InsightTriggerType { messageCount, inactivity }` + a `wireValue` extension mapping to `'message_count'`/`'inactivity'` (names don't match wire strings, unlike `EntrySource.name`).

+**Acceptance Criteria:**
+- Given either 5 user messages sent or 2 minutes of inactivity within the active Chat Session, when that condition is satisfied first, then `generateInsight` is called exactly once for that window — never both, never twice.

+/// spec-6-5 — a single proactively generated insight. Appended onto
+/// `ChatReady.activeInsight` as a plain nullable value (Intent: "never a
+/// second state container"), rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at
+/// the end of the message list. Plain value type, mirrors `ChatSession`:
+/// no `freezed`/`copyWith` machinery needed, manual `==`/`hashCode`/
+/// `toString`. Never persisted (Boundaries: "Never persist ChatInsight —
+/// no new Hive box").
+class ChatInsight {
+  const ChatInsight({required this.id, required this.content});
+
+  final String id;
+  final String content;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      identical(this, other) ||
+      (other is ChatInsight && other.id == id && other.content == content);
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(id, content);
+
+  @override
+  String toString() => 'ChatInsight(id: $id, content: $content)';
+}
+
+/// The two trigger conditions `ChatCubit`'s own per-session window races
+/// (Boundaries: "a counter ... and a Timer ... race; whichever hits its
+/// threshold first") — a fixed user-message count vs. a fixed inactivity
+/// timeout, whichever is satisfied first.
+enum InsightTriggerType { messageCount, inactivity }
+
+/// `chat-insight-create`'s own wire strings for [InsightTriggerType]
+/// (`openapi.yaml`'s `message_count`/`inactivity` enum) — the member
+/// names don't match them 1:1 (unlike `EntrySource.name`, which already
+/// matches the backend's lowercase strings verbatim), so this extension
+/// maps explicitly instead.
+extension InsightTriggerTypeWireValue on InsightTriggerType {
+  String get wireValue => switch (this) {
+    InsightTriggerType.messageCount => 'message_count',
+    InsightTriggerType.inactivity => 'inactivity',
+  };
+}

+                  crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42	
43	### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test
44	
45	For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.
46	
47	A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.
48	
49	Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.
50	
51	- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
52	- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
53	- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.
54	
55	A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.
56	
57	For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.
58	
59	Common patterns:
60	
61	- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
62	- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
63	- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
64	- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
65	- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
66	- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.
67	
68	### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real
69	
70	Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.
71	
72	Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.
73	
74	Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.
75	
76	Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.
77	
78	## OUTPUT FORMAT
79	
80	Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.
81	
82	```markdown
83	### <one-line title naming the gap>
84	
85	- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
86	- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
87	- **Existing test evidence:**
88	  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
89	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
90	  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
91	- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
92	- **Demonstration:**
93	  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
94	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
95	- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
96	- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
97	```
98	
99	If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:
100	
101	```markdown
102	## Other findings
103	
104	- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
105	```
106	
107	When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:
108	
109	`No verification gaps found.`
110	
111	## CONTENT SOURCE
112	
113	Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`
114

+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.
+
+**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Per active session: a counter (user messages sent via `sendMessage` only, never `retryMessage`) and a `Timer` (restarted on every `sendMessage` and every fire) race; whichever hits its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`, then immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves, so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
+- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** — the first caller not to await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await it).
+- A failure — transport `Left`, or a 200 with `status != 'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no overlay, no retry affordance.
+- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; the 3 existing direct `ChatReady(...)` constructions in `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already start it `null` — only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those sites.
+- `dismissInsight()` clears `activeInsight` via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (`copyWith`'s `??` can't express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` never clears instead of fixing `copyWith`); never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint in the contract) and never touches any other field.
+- An insight resolving after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved away is dropped (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches).
+- Insight card tokens (spine width, card padding, label spacing, dismiss icon size) go in `design_tokens.dart`, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
+
+**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight` shape, reset-before-fire ordering, and the `Duration` test seam are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").
+
+**Never:**
+- Never call the backend on dismiss, or show a card / surface `errorCode` for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
+- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
+- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository`.
+- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
+- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box, no cross-session reconciliation unlike bookmark state).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
+| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
+| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
+| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
+| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |

+
+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** The assistant never surfaces a pattern from the user's own history unprompted — `ChatRepository` has no insight-generation method, `ChatReady` has no slot for one, and nothing counts messages or idle time within a session.
+
+**Approach:** `ChatCubit` tracks a per-session trigger window (5 user messages sent OR 2 minutes idle, whichever first) and fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` (story 6.4's helper, its first unawaited caller) the instant the window closes, reopening a fresh window immediately. A successful, `status: 'ready'` result is appended onto `ChatReady` as a single nullable `activeInsight` value — rendered as the ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card at the end of the message list — never a second state container. Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is silently dropped.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- Per active session: a counter (user messages sent via `sendMessage` only, never `retryMessage`) and a `Timer` (restarted on every `sendMessage` and every fire) race; whichever hits its threshold first calls `generateInsight(sessionId, triggerType:, triggerKey:)`, then immediately resets the counter, generates a fresh `triggerKey`, and restarts the timer — before the network call resolves, so the window closes structurally and the other condition can never also fire for it.
+- The call goes through `isolatedSideEffect`, **unawaited** — the first caller not to await it (6.4's `bookmarkMessage` does await it).
+- A failure — transport `Left`, or a 200 with `status != 'ready'` (RF08: "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes `status='failed'`") — is dropped silently: no card, no overlay, no retry affordance.
+- `ChatReady.activeInsight` (nullable `ChatInsight`) is the only new state; the 3 existing direct `ChatReady(...)` constructions in `_bootstrap`/`switchSession`/`startNewSession` already start it `null` — only the counter/timer need an explicit reset call at those sites.
+- `dismissInsight()` clears `activeInsight` via a direct `ChatReady(...)` construction (`copyWith`'s `??` can't express "set to null", same reason `restoreScrollOffset` never clears instead of fixing `copyWith`); never calls the backend (no dismiss endpoint in the contract) and never touches any other field.
+- An insight resolving after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` moved away is dropped (`ChatReady.sessionId` no longer matches).
+- Insight card tokens (spine width, card padding, label spacing, dismiss icon size) go in `design_tokens.dart`, never hardcoded (AGENTS.md).
+
+**Ask First:** none — the single-nullable-`activeInsight` shape, reset-before-fire ordering, and the `Duration` test seam are reasonable technical decisions for a mechanism-only story (`docs/input/` silent on them; AGENTS.md: "decide and proceed").
+
+**Never:**
+- Never call the backend on dismiss, or show a card / surface `errorCode` for any `status` other than `'ready'`.
+- Never let the counter/timer leak across sessions.
+- Never route insight generation through `SaveChatMessageAsEntryUseCase`/`EntriesRepository`.
+- Never await the insight `isolatedSideEffect` call.
+- Never persist `ChatInsight` (no new Hive box, no cross-session reconciliation unlike bookmark state).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| 5th user message | `sendMessage()` called a 5th time within the current window | `message_count` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| 2 minutes idle | No `sendMessage()` call for the configured duration since the window opened | `inactivity` trigger fires once; counter/key reset, fresh timer starts | N/A |
+| Near-simultaneous | 5th message sent right as the inactivity timer would fire | Only `message_count` fires — sending synchronously cancels/restarts the timer first | N/A |
+| Generation fails | `generateInsight` resolves `Left` or `Right` with `status != 'ready'` | `activeInsight` stays null; composer/bubbles/chat unaffected | Silently dropped |
+| Session switched mid-flight | `switchSession`/`startNewSession` called while a call is pending | Result dropped on arrival — `sessionId` no longer matches | N/A |
+| Dismiss | `dismissInsight()` tapped | `activeInsight` → null; scroll position and every other field unchanged | N/A |
+| Dismiss with none active | `dismissInsight()` called while `activeInsight` is already null | No-op | N/A |

  - **The "INSIGHT" label is colored with `colorAccent`, directly violating the frozen requirement that the spine is the *only* accent-colored element.** `lib/features/chat/presentation/widgets/insight_card.dart`'s `Text('INSIGHT', style: DesignTokens.textMonoCaption.copyWith(color: DesignTokens.colorAccent))` colors the label itself. Both `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-6-context.md`'s UX & Interaction Patterns ("the spine is the only accent-colored element inside the chat stream itself") and spec-6-5's own frozen Acceptance Criteria ("as the only accent-colored element") say otherwise. The new `test/features/chat/presentation/widgets/insight_card_test.dart` even bakes the bug into its assertions, with a comment admitting "together with the spine, the two accent-colored surfaces this card ever shows" — the test was written to match the implementation instead of catching the spec violation.
  
  - **No guard against out-of-order/overlapping `generateInsight` results.** `ChatCubit._applyInsightResult` only checks `current.sessionId == sessionId`; it has no notion of which trigger/window a result belongs to. Because `_fireInsightTrigger` reopens a fresh window (and can start a brand-new unawaited request) immediately, before the previous request resolves, two in-flight calls for the same session can resolve out of order. A late-arriving older result can silently overwrite a newer `activeInsight`, or resurrect an insight the user already cleared via `dismissInsight()` — with nothing to drop it as stale. The I/O matrix only covers the single-session-switch staleness case, not this one.
  
  - **No test exercises concurrent/overlapping insight requests**, even though `chat_cubit_test.dart`'s fake (`generateInsightCalls` + per-call `_insightCompleters`) was clearly built to support resolving calls independently/out of order. Every test that uses it only ever has one pending completer at a time, so the overwrite/resurrection scenario above is untested.
  
  - **No expiry/anchoring policy for a visible, un-dismissed insight.** `chat_screen.dart`'s `itemBuilder` always renders the `InsightCard` at `index == messages.length` — i.e. glued to the current end of the list. If the user keeps chatting without tapping dismiss, the same (now stale) insight keeps sliding down to stay pinned under each new message indefinitely, detached from the conversational moment it was generated for. Neither the Boundaries nor the I/O matrix say what should happen to a still-visible insight once the conversation moves on.
  
  - **Doc/value mismatch in the new design token.** `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`'s `chatInsightCardPadding` doc says the value is "`chatBubblePadding`'s horizontal value on the trailing/vertical edges" (`chatBubblePadding`'s horizontal is `spacingMd` = 16), but the actual vertical padding chosen is `14`, not `16`. The stated rationale doesn't match the number it documents.
  
  - **New off-grid magic numbers with no acknowledged tradeoff.** The `14.0` vertical padding and `6.0` label spacing fall outside the project's documented 4dp spacing grid (`spacingXs 4 / spacingSm 8 / spacingMd 16 / spacingLg 24 / spacingXl 32`). `chatBubblePadding`'s own comment explicitly flags its one off-grid value ("vertical isn't on the 4dp scale") as a conscious choice; the new tokens introduce more off-grid values with no equivalent justification, eroding the single-source-of-truth discipline `design_tokens.dart` is meant to enforce.

That holds today, but nothing in the type system stops a future refactor from firing a request with `triggerKey: ''`, which would violate `openapi.yaml`'s `minLength: 1` on that field.
  
  - **The spec's Code Map under-scoped this story's actual blast radius.** Making every bootstrapped `ChatCubit` always start a live inactivity `Timer` broke the pending-timers invariant in three test files never listed anywhere in spec-6-5's Code Map: `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart`, and `test/main_test.dart` — all of which needed new workaround code purely because they happen to construct a real `ChatCubit` for unrelated reasons (routing/drawer tests). The Code Map lists exactly 5 test files; the diff touches 8.
  
  - **The workaround for that is copy-pasted four times instead of shared.** `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `main_test.dart`, and `chat_screen_test.dart` each define their own near-identical local `testWidgets(...)` override (`hide`/`show` the real one, close pending `ChatCubit`s in a `finally` block before the framework's `!timersPending` check runs) — the same boilerplate and the same multi-line rationale comment repeated four times rather than factored into one shared test helper.
  
  - **New timing-based tests lean on real wall-clock timers with thin margins.** E.g. a `20ms` configured inactivity timeout checked after only `150ms`, and a `500ms` timeout race double-checked with just a `50ms` follow-up wait (`chat_cubit_test.dart`'s "proactive insight" group). This is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (no `fake_async` dependency added), but it's a real flakiness exposure under CI load that the rest of the suite doesn't carry, and it's worth flagging even though it was a conscious decision.
  
  - **Formatting drift in `chat_screen.dart`.** The line `itemCount: messages.length + (activeInsight != null ? 1 : 0),` runs to ~83 columns at its actual indentation, while every surrounding line in the same file is wrapped to stay well under 80. Not caught by `flutter analyze`, but inconsistent with the rest of the file's formatting discipline (and would be reflowed by `dart format`).
  
  - **Silent insight failures compound with the backend's "never an HTTP error" design with no visibility anywhere.** Because `chat-insight-create` always answers HTTP 200 even on failure (RF08), an `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` insight failure never reaches any transport-level 401 handling the app might have elsewhere; every subsequent window will keep silently failing the same way until something unrelated refreshes the token. </agent-message>

Because `_fireInsightTrigger` reopens a fresh window (and can start a brand-new unawaited request) immediately, before the previous request resolves, two in-flight calls for the same session can resolve out of order. A late-arriving older result can silently overwrite a newer `activeInsight`, or resurrect an insight the user already cleared via `dismissInsight()` — with nothing to drop it as stale. The I/O matrix only covers the single-session-switch staleness case, not this one.
  
  - **No test exercises concurrent/overlapping insight requests**, even though `chat_cubit_test.dart`'s fake (`generateInsightCalls` + per-call `_insightCompleters`) was clearly built to support resolving calls independently/out of order. Every test that uses it only ever has one pending completer at a time, so the overwrite/resurrection scenario above is untested.
  
  - **No expiry/anchoring policy for a visible, un-dismissed insight.** `chat_screen.dart`'s `itemBuilder` always renders the `InsightCard` at `index == messages.length` — i.e. glued to the current end of the list. If the user keeps chatting without tapping dismiss, the same (now stale) insight keeps sliding down to stay pinned under each new message indefinitely, detached from the conversational moment it was generated for. Neither the Boundaries nor the I/O matrix say what should happen to a still-visible insight once the conversation moves on.
  
  - **Doc/value mismatch in the new design token.** `lib/core/design_tokens.dart`'s `chatInsightCardPadding` doc says the value is "`chatBubblePadding`'s horizontal value on the trailing/vertical edges" (`chatBubblePadding`'s horizontal is `spacingMd` = 16), but the actual vertical padding chosen is `14`, not `16`. The stated rationale doesn't match the number it documents.
  
  - **New off-grid magic numbers with no acknowledged tradeoff.** The `14.0` vertical padding and `6.0` label spacing fall outside the project's documented 4dp spacing grid (`spacingXs 4 / spacingSm 8 / spacingMd 16 / spacingLg 24 / spacingXl 32`). `chatBubblePadding`'s own comment explicitly flags its one off-grid value ("vertical isn't on the 4dp scale") as a conscious choice; the new tokens introduce more off-grid values with no equivalent justification, eroding the single-source-of-truth discipline `design_tokens.dart` is meant to enforce.
  
  - **`_insightTriggerKey` has no structural non-empty guarantee.** It's a plain mutable `String` initialized to `''` in `ChatCubit`, relying entirely on every code path calling `_resetInsightWindow` before `_fireInsightTrigger` reads it. That holds today, but nothing in the type system stops a future refactor from firing a request with `triggerKey: ''`, which would violate `openapi.yaml`'s `minLength: 1` on that field.
  
  - **The spec's Code Map under-scoped this story's actual blast radius.** Making every bootstrapped `ChatCubit` always start a live inactivity `Timer` broke the pending-timers invariant in three test files never listed anywhere in spec-6-5's Code Map: `test/core/navigation/app_router_test.dart`, `test/core/widgets/app_drawer_test.dart`, and `test/main_test.dart` — all of which needed new workaround code purely because they happen to construct a real `ChatCubit` for unrelated reasons (routing/drawer tests). The Code Map lists exactly 5 test files; the diff touches 8.
  
  - **The workaround for that is copy-pasted four times instead of shared.** `app_router_test.dart`, `app_drawer_test.dart`, `main_test.dart`, and `chat_screen_test.dart` each define their own near-identical local `testWidgets(...)` override (`hide`/`show` the real one, close pending `ChatCubit`s in a `finally` block before the framework's `!timersPending` check runs) — the same boilerplate and the same multi-line rationale comment repeated four times rather than factored into one shared test helper.
  
  - **New timing-based tests lean on real wall-clock timers with thin margins.** E.g. a `20ms` configured inactivity timeout checked after only `150ms`, and a `500ms` timeout race double-checked with just a `50ms` follow-up wait (`chat_cubit_test.dart`'s "proactive insight" group). This is a deliberate, documented tradeoff (no `fake_async` dependency added), but it's a real flakiness exposure under CI load that the rest of the suite doesn't carry, and it's worth flagging even though it was a conscious decision.
  
  - **Formatting drift in `chat_screen.dart`.** The line `itemCount: messages.length + (activeInsight != null ? 1 : 0),` runs to ~83 columns at its actual indentation, while every surrounding line in the same file is wrapped to stay well under 80. Not caught by `flutter analyze`, but inconsistent with the rest of the file's formatting discipline (and would be reflowed by `dart format`).
  
  - **Silent insight failures compound with the backend's "never an HTTP error" design with no visibility anywhere.** Because `chat-insight-create` always answers HTTP 200 even on failure (RF08), an `AUTH_EXPIRED`/`AUTH_INVALID` insight failure never reaches any transport-level 401 handling the app might have elsewhere; every subsequent window will keep silently failing the same way until something unrelated refreshes the token. This is consistent with the frozen Boundaries ("silently dropped"), but it's a real user-facing consequence (the feature can go dark indefinitely with zero signal, even to logs) that nothing in the spec or diff accounts for.

## RULES

- **Language** — Speak in `English`. Write any file output in `English`.
- NEVER auto-push.

## INSTRUCTIONS

### Generate Suggested Review Order

Read `{baseline_commit}` from `{spec_file}` frontmatter and construct the diff of all changes since that commit.

Append the review order as a `## Suggested Review Order` section to `{spec_file}` **after the last existing section**. Do not modify the Code Map.

Build the trail as an ordered sequence of **stops** — clickable `path:line` references with brief framing — optimized for a human reviewer reading top-down to understand the change:

1. **Order by concern, not by file.** Group stops by the conceptual concern they address (e.g., "validation logic", "schema change", "UI binding"). A single file may appear under multiple concerns.
2. **Lead with the entry point** — the single highest-leverage file:line a reviewer should look at first to grasp the design intent.
3. **Inside each concern**, order stops from most important / architecturally interesting to supporting. Lightly bias toward higher-risk or boundary-crossing stops.
4. **End with peripherals** — tests, config, types, and other supporting changes come last.
5. **Every code reference is a clickable spec-file-relative link.** Compute each link target as a relative path from `{spec_file}`'s directory to the changed file. Format each stop as a markdown link: `[short-name:line](../../path/to/file.ts#L42)`. Use a `#L` line anchor. Use the file's basename (or shortest unambiguous suffix) plus line number as the link text. The relative path must be dynamically derived — never hardcode the depth.
6. **Each stop gets one ultra-concise line of framing** (≤15 words) — why this approach was chosen here and what it achieves in the context of the change. No paragraphs.

Format each stop as framing first, link on the next indented line:

```markdown
## Suggested Review Order

**{Concern name}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:42`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L42)

- {one-line framing}
  [`other.ts:17`](../../src/path/to/other.ts#L17)

**{Next concern}**

- {one-line framing}
  [`file.ts:88`](../../src/path/to/file.ts#L88)
```

> The `../../` prefix above is illustrative — compute the actual relative path from `{spec_file}`'s directory to each target file.

When there is only one concern, omit the bold label — just list the stops directly.

content.text:
Opened successfully. Here's the summary:

## Story 6.5 — Proactive Insight Injection & Failure Isolation — done

**Commit:** `add1403` on `main`

**What shipped:**
- A per-session trigger window on `ChatCubit` — a message counter + `Timer`, racing — fires `ChatRepository.generateInsight()` fire-and-forget through `isolatedSideEffect` the instant 5 user messages or 2 minutes of idle time elapse, whichever comes first, then immediately reopens a fresh window.
- Any failure (transport or in-payload `status != 'ready'`) is dropped silently — no error, composer stays enabled, ordinary chat unaffected.
- A successful insight lands on one new `ChatReady.activeInsight` field, rendered as the trailing item in the message list (ochre-spine "INSIGHT" card, dismissible, no backend call on dismiss).

**Review findings and fixes applied** (3 parallel adversarial reviews against the full diff):
- The "INSIGHT" label was colored with the accent color, violating the frozen "spine is the only accent-colored element" rule — fixed, and the test that had baked the bug in was corrected to actually assert the invariant.
- No guard against two overlapping trigger windows resolving out of order — a stale result could have overwritten a newer insight or resurrected one the user already dismissed. Added a request-sequence guard in `ChatCubit`, with two new regression tests.
- A misleading doc comment, a duplicated `testWidgets`-plus-cleanup helper copy-pasted across 4 test files (now shared via `test/support/testwidgets_with_cleanup.dart`), and one formatting-drift line — all fixed.
- Six other findings reviewed and rejected as noise or already-accepted, documented tradeoffs (full reasoning is in my earlier message).

All patches re-verified: `flutter analyze` clean, 74 + 107 tests passing across every touched file.

The spec file is open in VS Code with a **Suggested Review Order** section — Cmd+click the links to jump through the change by concern (trigger window → state shape → repository mapping → UI → tests).
